arxiv-2101-11212.creator: Muhammad Asif Ali, 1 Yifang Sun, 1 Bing Li, 1 Wei Wang, 2 1 School of Computer Science and Engineering, UNSW, Australia 2 The Hong Kong university of Science and Technology, China {muhammadasif.ali, bing.li, yifangs}@unsw.edu.au, {weiwcs}@ust.hk
arxiv-2101-11212.description: Abstract . Fine-Grained Named Entity Typing ( FG-NET ) aims at classifying the entity mentions into a wide range of entity types (usually hundreds) depending upon the context. While distant supervision is the most common way to acquire supervised training data, it brings in label noise, as it assigns type labels to the entity mentions irrespective of mentions’ context.

arxiv-2206-08993.title: A bijection between K K -Kohnert diagrams and reverse set-valued tableaux
arxiv-2206-08993.creator: Jianping Pan, Tianyi Yu
arxiv-2206-08993.description: Abstract . Lascoux polynomials are K K -theoretic analogues of the key polynomials. They both have combinatorial formulas involving tableaux: reverse set-valued tableaux ( 𝖱𝖲𝖵𝖳 \mathsf{RSVT} ) rule for Lascoux polynomials and reverse semistandard Young tableaux ( 𝖱𝖲𝖲𝖸𝖳 \mathsf{RSSYT} ) rule for key polynomials.

arxiv-2304-07380.title: Quantum fluctuations induce collective multiphonons in finite Fermi liquids
arxiv-2304-07380.creator: Petar Marević, David Regnier, Denis Lacroix
arxiv-2304-07380.description: Abstract We show that collective multiphonon states in atomic nuclei emerge at high excitation energies when quantum fluctuations in the collective space are included beyond the independent-particle approximation. The quadrupole response of a nucleus is studied using an extension of the nuclear time-dependent density-functional theory that mixes several many-body trajectories.

arxiv-2309-06377.title: Adversarial attacks on hybrid classical-quantum Deep Learning models for Histopathological Cancer Detection
arxiv-2309-06377.creator: Biswaraj Baral, Reek Majumdar, Bhavika Bhalgamiya, Taposh Dutta Roy
arxiv-2309-06377.description: Abstract We present an effective application of quantum machine learning in histopathological cancer detection. The study here emphasizes two primary applications of hybrid classical-quantum Deep Learning models. The first application is to build a classification model for histopathological cancer detection using the quantum transfer learning strategy.

arxiv-2403-10898.title: Role of Coulomb interaction in the valley photogalvanic effect
arxiv-2403-10898.creator: V. M. Kovalev, A. V. Parafilo, O. V. Kibis, I. G. Savenko
arxiv-2403-10898.description: Abstract We develop a theory of Coulomb interaction-related contribution to the photogalvanic current of the carriers of charge in two-dimensional non-centrosymmetric Dirac materials possessing a nontrivial structure of valleys and exposed to an external electromagnetic field. The valley photogalvanic effect occurs here due to the trigonal warping of electrons and holes’ dispersions in a given valley of the monolayer.

arxiv-2405-14575.title: Share-Based Fairness for Arbitrary Entitlements
arxiv-2405-14575.creator: Moshe Babaioff, Uriel Feige
arxiv-2405-14575.description: Abstract We consider the problem of fair allocation of indivisible items to agents that have arbitrary entitlements to the items. Every agent i i has a valuation function v i v_{i} and an entitlement b i b_{i} , where entitlements sum up to 1.

arxiv-2409-12999.title: Impact of Grain Boundary Energy Anisotropy on Grain Growth
arxiv-2409-12999.creator: S. Kiana Naghibzadeh, Zipeng Xu, David Kinderlehrer, Robert Suter, Kaushik Dayal, Gregory S. Rohrer
arxiv-2409-12999.description: Abstract A threshold dynamics model of grain growth that accounts for the anisotropy in the grain boundary energy has been used to simulate experimentally observed grain growth of polycrystalline Ni. The simulation reproduces several aspects of the observed microstructural evolution that are not found in the results of simulations assuming isotropic properties.

arxiv-2411-02441.title: Cross-D Conv : Cross-Dimensional Transferable Knowledge Base via Fourier Shifting Operation
arxiv-2411-02441.creator: Mehmet Can Yavuz, Yang Yang
arxiv-2411-02441.description: Abstract In biomedical imaging analysis, the dichotomy between 2D and 3D data presents a significant challenge. While 3D volumes offer superior real-world applicability, they are less available for each modality and not easy to train in large scale, whereas 2D samples are abundant but less comprehensive.

arxiv-2511-09423.title: Pseudo-Differential Operators and Generalized Random Fields over Tori
arxiv-2511-09423.creator: Nicolas Escobar
arxiv-2511-09423.description: Abstract Matérn covariance functions are ubiquitous in spatial statistics, valued for their interpretable parameters and well-understood sample path properties in Euclidean settings. This paper examines whether these desirable properties transfer to manifold domains through rigorous analysis of Matérn processes on tori using pseudo-differential operator theory.

arxiv-2512-13957.title: From ASTRID to BRAHMA - The role of overmassive black holes in little red dots in cosmological simulations ∗ E-mail:plachance@cmu.edu
arxiv-2512-13957.creator: Patrick LaChance 1,∗, Aklant Kumar Bhowmick 2,3,4, Rupert A.C. Croft 1, Tiziana Di Matteo 1, Yihao Zhou 1, Fabio Pacucci 5,6, Laura Blecha 7, Paul Torrey 2,3,4, Yueying Ni 8, Nianyi Chen 9, Simeon Bird 10
arxiv-2512-13957.description: Abstract We leverage the overmassive black holes ( M BH / M ∗ ≈ 0.1 \rm M_{BH}/M_{\ast}\approx 0.1 ) present in a realization of the BRAHMA cosmological hydrodynamic simulation suite to investigate their role in the emission of the unique “little red dot” (LRD) objects identified by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST).

pmc-11430573.title: Immunolocalization of Aquaporin 1, 2, and 9 in Anuran Testis of the Neotropical Pointedbelly Frog Leptodactylus podicipinus
pmc-11430573.creator: Rafael O A Bordin, Classius de Oliveira, Raquel F Domeniconi, Huafeng Wang
pmc-11430573.description: Many anuran survival strategies involve hydric regulation, and reproduction is not different. The aquaporin (AQP) family plays an important role in water transport and regulation in many tissues, including the male gonad. The testes undergo various stages of change during the reproductive cycle, and water balance is an important factor for ensuring reproductive success.

pmc-11586650.title: Direct Observations of Coastally Generated Near‐Inertial Waves During a Wind Event
pmc-11586650.creator: Samuel M. Kelly, Erica L. Green, Ian A. Stokes, Jay A. Austin, Andrew J. Lucas, Jonathan D. Nash
pmc-11586650.description: Wind over the ocean generates near‐inertial velocities. In the open ocean, horizontal variability in the inertial frequency and mesoscale vorticity generate internal waves that transport energy laterally and drive diapcynal mixing in remote locations. In the coastal ocean, horizontal variability is produced by the coastline.

pmc-11670049.title: Targeting specific brain districts for advanced nanotherapies: A review from the perspective of precision nanomedicine
pmc-11670049.creator: Giulia Sierri, Michela Patrucco, Davide Ferrario, Antonio Renda, Susanna Comi, Matilde Ciprandi, Veronica Fontanini, Francesco Saverio Sica, Silvia Sesana, Marta Costa Verdugo, Marcelo Kravicz, Luca Salassa, Marta Busnelli, Francesca Re
pmc-11670049.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Numerous studies are focused on nanoparticle penetration into the brain functionalizing them with ligands useful to cross the blood–brain barrier. However, cell targeting is also crucial, given that cerebral pathologies frequently affect specific brain cells or areas. Functionalize nanoparticles with the most appropriate targeting elements, tailor their physical parameters, and consider the brain's complex anatomy are essential aspects for precise therapy and diagnosis.

pmc-12735136.title: Role of Açaí (Euterpe oleracea) in Modulating the Immune Response During Experimental Oral Infection with Trypanosoma cruzi
pmc-12735136.creator: Flávia de Souza Marques, Thays Helena Chaves Duarte, Viviane Flores Xavier, Aline Coelho das Mercês, Thaís Vieira de Carvalho Silva, Luciana da Fonseca Medeiros, Camilo Elber Vital, Cláudia Martins Carneiro, William de Castro Borges, Paula Melo de Abreu Vieira, Giovanni Sgroi
pmc-12735136.description: Oral infection is now the main route of Chagas disease transmission in endemic countries, with açaí (Euterpe oleracea) being the primary food involved in Brazil. However, the role of açaí in parasite–host interaction remains largely unexplored. This study assessed the effect of açaí inoculum on experimental Trypanosoma cruzi infection.

pmc-13576219.title: “People are going to do drugs:” harm reduction as a strategy for survivors of sex trafficking who use substances
pmc-13576219.creator: Lindsay B Gezinski, Ariel M S Richer, Aundrea Dilanchian, Theresa Anasti, Nathaniel A Dell, Cassandra Price
pmc-13576219.description: BackgroundSurvivors of sex trafficking often experience co-occurring substance use and face significant barriers to accessing care. Harm reduction offers a nonjudgmental, survivor-centered approach to mitigating health risks associated with substance use and commercial sex. However, limited research has explored how harm reduction is understood and implemented by service providers working with this population.

pmc-13585947.title: Effects of recumbency and tube current on image quality of canine elbow computed tomography
pmc-13585947.creator: S. R. Bellekom, M. Dekkers, M. Beukers
pmc-13585947.description: BackgroundElbow dysplasia is a leading cause of forelimb lameness in medium- to large-breed dogs, and computed tomography (CT) is the imaging modality of choice for assessment of the medial coronoid process. Image quality depends on patient positioning and tube current, but their effects have not been systematically compared.
